simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-01.title: Group cleverly
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-01.body:
Match each number with a number to subtract:

$(7 - 7) + (16 - 6) + (34 - 4) + (45 - 15) + 50 = 0 + 10 + 30 + 30 + 50 = 120$.

**Answer: (B) 120**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-01.title: Add, then subtract
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-01.body:
Add the plus numbers: $7 + 16 + 34 + 45 + 50 = 152$. Add the minus numbers: $6 + 15 + 4 + 7 = 32$. $152 - 32 = 120$.

**Answer: (B) 120**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-02.title: Three patterns mixed together
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-02.body:
Look at every third circle:

- 1st, 4th, 7th circles: 1 black & 1 white, 2 black & 2 white, 3 black & 3 white.
- 2nd, 5th, 8th circles: 10, 8, 6 black.
- 3rd, 6th, 9th circles: 2, 3, 4 white.

The circle with the question mark is the 10th, which continues the first pattern: 4 black & 4 white. So it has 4 black circles.

**Answer: (D) 4**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-02.title: Check the neighbours
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-02.body:
The 7th circle has 3 black and 3 white dots and the pattern of the 1st, 4th, 7th circles grows by one of each colour every time. The 10th circle is next in that list: 4 black, 4 white.

**Answer: (D) 4**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-03.title: Smallest and largest
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-03.body:
The smallest sum is $1 + 1 + 1 = 3$ and the largest is $6 + 6 + 6 = 18$. 22 is more than 18, so it is impossible.

**Answer: (D) 22**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-04.title: Count the lines from above
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-04.body:
Imagine looking straight down on the figure. Its top view is a long rectangle crossed by the edges of the blocks: counting all the vertical lines (including the two ends) there are **3** of them, and the circle of the cylinder appears in the correct part.

All the other options have 4 vertical lines, so only C can be the top view.

**Answer: (C)**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-05.title: Fill in the places
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-05.body:
Mitchell is one place behind the winner, so Mitchell is 2nd. Mark is directly ahead of Jason, so they must be 3rd and 4th (the 1st–2nd pair is taken by the winner and Mitchell). So the winner is the remaining runner: Tom.

Order: Tom, Mitchell, Mark, Jason.

**Answer: (C) Tom**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-05.title: Rule people out
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-05.body:
Mitchell can't win (he is behind the winner). Jason can't win (Mark is ahead of him). If Mark won, Jason would be 2nd — but Mitchell is 2nd. So Tom wins.

**Answer: (C) Tom**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-06.title: Multiply
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-06.body:
Each of the 5 colours comes with 2 door options: $5 \times 2 = 10$ versions.

**Answer: (A) 10**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-06.title: List
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-06.body:
Blue 2-door, blue 4-door, white 2-door, white 4-door, yellow 2-door, yellow 4-door, black 2-door, black 4-door, red 2-door, red 4-door — 10.

**Answer: (A) 10**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-07.title: Flip left and right
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-07.body:
In a mirror image everything that pointed right now points left, but up and down stay the same. The rocket at the top points up-right, so its mirror image points up-left, with the star, windows and flames in the flipped positions.

Comparing details (the star, the windows, the fins and the flames), options B, C, D and E each have some part that is not a correct flip. Only A matches.

**Answer: (A)**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-08.title: Digit sum
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-08.body:
For divisibility by 3 the digit sum $3 + 2 + B + 9 = 14 + B$ must be a multiple of 3. So $B = 1, 4$ or $7$. The only even one is $B = 4$.

**Answer: (C) 4**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-09.title: Compare the two baskets
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-09.body:
Second basket: 1 cat + 1 sheep need 5 balloons.

First basket: 1 cat + 1 sheep + 2 dogs need 11 balloons. Taking away the cat and the sheep (5 balloons), 2 dogs need 6 balloons, so 1 dog needs 3.

Sheep + cat + dog: $5 + 3 = 8$ balloons.

**Answer: (A) 8**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-09.title: Half-way
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-09.body:
The third basket has one dog fewer than the first basket. The two dogs needed $11 - 5 = 6$ balloons, so removing one dog removes 3 balloons: $11 - 3 = 8$.

**Answer: (A) 8**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-10.title: Try both orders
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-10.body:
**Four Princesses first:** 10:00 to 11:55. The next Dragon Fighter show is 14:10, ending 14:10 + 1 h 45 min = 15:55.

**Dragon Fighter first:** the 9:00 show is missed, so 10:55 to 12:40. The next Four Princesses show is 13:55, ending 13:55 + 1 h 55 min = 15:50.

The earliest finish is 15:50.

**Answer: (C) 15:50**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-11.title: Row rule
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-11.body:
In each row, the third picture is made by putting the first picture on top of the second picture and then removing the smallest circle.

Third row: the six-pointed star placed on the double circle, with the small inner circle removed, gives option B.

**Answer: (B)**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-12.title: Find the size of one square
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-12.body:
Count squares: the figures have 10, 12, 8 and 11 squares. The largest area is the one with 12 squares, so each square has area $48 \div 12 = 4$ cm² and side 2 cm.

Count the outside edges (in square sides): 16, 16, 24 and 16. The third figure has the largest perimeter: $24 \times 2 = 48$ cm.

**Answer: (D) 48 cm**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-12.title: Perimeter by edges
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-12.body:
Each square has side 2 cm (from $2 \times 2 = 4$ cm² and $12 \times 4 = 48$). The zig-zag figure has 24 unit edges around its boundary, the others only 16. $24 \times 2 = 48$ cm.

**Answer: (D) 48 cm**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-13.title: Count the days
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-13.body:
From 102 pages down to 4 pages she drops $102 - 4 = 98$ pages, 2 per day, so it happens $98 \div 2 = 49$ days after the first Saturday.

49 days is exactly 7 weeks, so it is again a **Saturday** — not among A–D.

**Answer: (E) None of the above** (Saturday)

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-13.title: Week by week
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-13.body:
Each week she reads 14 pages less on the same weekday. Saturdays: 102, 88, 74, 60, 46, 32, 18, 4. So she reads 4 pages on a Saturday.

**Answer: (E)**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-14.title: Multiples of 6
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-14.body:
A number divisible by both 2 and 3 is a multiple of 6. Multiples of 6 up to 99: $99 \div 6 = 16$ remainder 3, so 16 of them; one of those (6) is a one-digit number. $16 - 1 = 15$.

**Answer: (C) 15**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-15.title: Compare in pairs
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-15.body:
- 2 trains balance 3 cars, so a train is heavier than a car.
- 4 cars balance 5 ships, so a car is heavier than a ship.
- 3 submarines balance 4 trains, so a submarine is heavier than a train.

From lightest to heaviest: ship, car, train, submarine.

**Answer: (B) Submarine**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-15.title: Fewer means heavier
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-15.body:
On each balance, the side with fewer toys has the heavier toys. Submarine beats train (3 vs 4), train beats car (2 vs 3), car beats ship (4 vs 5). The submarine is heaviest.

**Answer: (B) Submarine**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-16.title: Count by size
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-16.body:
Count the rectangles (squares count too) by how many small rectangles they are made of:

- 1-part: 16
- 2-part: 10
- 3-part: 1
- 4-part: 3

Total $16 + 10 + 1 + 3 = 30$.

**Answer: 30**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-17.title: Find the rule
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-17.body:
Write the answer as two parts: the first part is twice the left number, and the second part is twice the difference of the two numbers.

- $2 \circledast 4$: $2 \times 2 = 4$ and $2 \times (4 - 2) = 4$ → 44 ✓
- $5 \circledast 7$: $10$ and $4$ → 104 ✓
- $1 \circledast 5$: $2$ and $8$ → 28 ✓
- $7 \circledast 10$: $14$ and $6$ → 146 ✓

So $6 \circledast 12$: $12$ and $2 \times 6 = 12$ → **1212**.

**Answer: 1212**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-17.title: Why this rule
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-17.body:
The last digit in each answer is always even and equals twice the gap ($4 - 2 = 2$ → 4, $7 - 5 = 2$ → 4, $5 - 1 = 4$ → 8, $10 - 7 = 3$ → 6), and what is written before it is twice the first number (4, 10, 2, 14). Following the same rule for 6 and 12 gives 12 followed by 12.

**Answer: 1212**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-18.title: Count pictures
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-18.body:
Pictures: Anastacia 1, Braiden 7, Clarke 8, Darla 4, Eddie 4, total 24. Each picture is 6 muffins, so there are $24 \times 6 = 144$ muffins.

Shared among 4 children: $144 \div 4 = 36$ each. Eddie had $4 \times 6 = 24$, so he has $36 - 24 = 12$ more.

**Answer: 12**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-18.title: Work in pictures
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-18.body:
24 pictures shared among 4 children is 6 pictures each. Eddie had 4 pictures, so he gains 2 pictures $= 2 \times 6 = 12$ muffins.

**Answer: 12**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-19.title: Model method
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-19.body:
Let Kim have 1 unit. Shaun has 2 units, Andrew has 2 units − 24.

$5$ units $- 24 = 256$, so 5 units $= 280$ and 1 unit $= 56$.

Andrew: $2 \times 56 - 24 = 112 - 24 = 88$.

**Answer: 88**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-20.title: Simplify
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-20.body:
6 boxes minus 1 box is 5 boxes: $\square \times 5 + 13 = 63$.

$\square \times 5 = 50$, so $\square = 10$.

**Answer: 10**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-21.title: Model method
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-21.body:
Let the hundreds digit be 1 unit. Tens = 2 units, ones = 1 unit − 1.

$4$ units $- 1 = 15$, so 4 units $= 16$ and 1 unit $= 4$.

Hundreds 4, tens 8, ones 3: **483**.

**Answer: 483**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-21.title: Try hundreds digits
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-21.body:
The tens digit is twice the hundreds digit, so the hundreds digit is 1–4. Try: 1 → 120 (sum 3), 2 → 241 (sum 7), 3 → 362 (sum 11), 4 → 483 (sum 15 ✓).

**Answer: 483**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-22.title: Try numbers of adults
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-22.body:
Try 11 adults down: 11 → \$88, leaving \$2 ✗; 10 → \$10 left ✗; 9 → \$18 ✗; 8 → \$26 ✗; 7 → \$34 ✗; 6 → \$42 $= 6 \times \$7$ ✓.

So 6 adults and 6 children, 12 people (fewer than 14 ✓).

**Answer: 6**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-22.title: Why there is only one answer
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-22.body:
If everyone paid \$7, $n$ people would pay $7n$; each adult adds \$1. So $90 = 7 \times (\text{people}) + (\text{adults})$. With fewer than 14 people: 12 people gives $84 + 6$ → 6 adults ✓; 11 people would need 13 adults ✗; 13 people would need $-1$ adults ✗.

**Answer: 6**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-23.title: Pages 1–99, then 100–130
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-23.body:
Pages 1–99: ten 1s in the ones place and ten in the tens place → 20.

Pages 100–130: 31 hundreds-digit 1s, plus ones-digit 1s in 101, 111, 121 (3), plus tens-digit 1s in 110–119 (10) → 44.

$20 + 44 = 64$.

**Answer: 64**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-24.title: Set up the equations
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-24.body:
Call the empty boxes in Picture 3: top row $A \times 2 = B$, middle row $7 \times C = D$. The columns say $A \times 7 = E$, $2 \times C = {?}$ and $B + D = 53$; the bottom row says $E - {?} = 53$.

So $2A + 7C = 53$ and $7A - 2C = 53$.

$7A$ is more than 53, so $A \ge 8$. $A = 8$: $7C = 37$ ✗. $A = 9$: $7C = 35$, $C = 5$, and $63 - 10 = 53$ ✓.

So ${?} = 2 \times 5 = 10$.

**Answer: 10**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-24.title: Check the whole grid
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-24.body:
Top row $9 \times 2 = 18$, middle row $7 \times 5 = 35$, columns $9 \times 7 = 63$, $2 \times 5 = 10$, $18 + 35 = 53$, bottom row $63 - 10 = 53$ ✓.

**Answer: 10**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-25.title: Rewrite as an addition
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-25.body:
$ABBB - CCC = A$ means $CCC + A = ABBB$. A 3-digit number plus one digit is less than 1009, so $A = 1$.

Then $CCC + 1 = 1BBB$: the only 3-digit number which becomes a 4-digit number after adding 1 is 999, so $C = 9$ and $1BBB = 1000$, $B = 0$.

$A + B + C = 1 + 0 + 9 = 10$.

**Answer: 10**

simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-25.title: Check
simcc-sasmo-2019-g3-25.body:
$1000 - 999 = 1$ ✓ and the digits 1, 0, 9 are all different.

**Answer: 10**
